blind_target.title: The Effects of Personal Canvassing, Telephone Calls, and Direct Mail on Voter Turnout: A Field Experiment.
blind_target.evidence_quote: Returning to the original data files, we reconstructed both the household-level and the individual-level New Haven study for purposes of preparing this correction.
blind_target.outcome_computational_quote: Looking first at the model without covariates, we see that the estimated effect of face-to-face canvassing changes from 8.7 (published) to 8.4 (corrected). Mail’s effect changes from 0.58 (published) to 0.51 (corrected). The coefficient estimate for phone calls remains negative. The published value of −4.7 is corrected to be −1.9.
blind_target.outcome_robustness_quote: Correcting the coding errors in the New Haven study changes none of the substantive conclusions that flow from it.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: Reconstructing and correcting original data changes the reported coefficients beyond rounding (notably the telephone estimate), while the authors explicitly find the substantive conclusions unchanged under corrections and sample/model variations. New 2002 sample evidence separately confirms the original null telephone result; it is not used to decide the robustness axis.

blind_target.authors: Walton H, Jr, Miller CM and McCormick II JP
blind_target.title: Race and political science: the dual traditions of race relations politics and African-American politics
blind_target.evidence_quote:
We adopt the authors’ typology for distinguishing RRP
and AAP papers, and readers should consult the reference
lists in Walton et al. (1995: Appendix 1) for details.
blind_target.outcome_computational_quote:
By building an instrument that gets at
what Walton and his colleagues observe, we re-analyze
their corpus of text in novel ways and apply our instrument
to current articles in top-tier political science journals.
blind_target.outcome_robustness_quote:
This
replication-and-extension confirms not only that ours and
Walton’s operationalizations are empirically comparable
but also that the former can serve as a proxy for the
latter when reviewing the race literature.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: The original 54-publication corpus is re-analyzed using an alternative automated measure of centrality, rather than rerunning the original numerical analysis. The authors explicitly conclude the operationalizations are comparable and the original findings hold up to re-examination. New journal articles in the extension are not treated as robustness tests of original data.

shipped.title_o: Weak support for a U-shaped pattern between societal gender equality and fertility when comparing societies across time
shipped.outcome_quote: The analysis identifies a conditional U-shaped relationship between gender equality and fertility

blind_target.title: Weak support for a U-shaped pattern between societal gender equality and fertility when comparing societies across time
blind_target.evidence_quote: Kolk’s (2019) original analysis was based on Stata software; in this study, I try to replicate Kolk’s (2019) finding in R version 4.1.3. Specifically, I replicate Figures 1, 2, and 3 in Kolk’s original paper.
blind_target.outcome_computational_quote: My replication is almost identical to Kolk’s original study. The overall negative association and U-shaped relationship between the TFR and the WPEI after 2000 is noticeable in both visualisations (shown in the Appendix). However, there are also some small differences between my replication and Kolk’s (2019) results.
blind_target.outcome_robustness_quote: The main finding of this study is that in contrast to Kolk’s (2019) conclusion of weak support, conditional support for a U-shaped relationship between gender equality and fertility in developed countries emerges when a more comprehensive gender equality indicator is employed in the analysis. Although Kolk’s (2019) study demonstrates a high level of verifiability and low inaccuracy (as shown in the Appendix), his results appear to be sensitive to the choice of gender-equality indicator.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: Appendix reconstructs the original historical aggregate-data analysis and obtains nearly identical results; the author describes discrepancies as small and overall inaccuracy as minimal. Classified computationally reproducible under the negligible-difference allowance, with uncertainty because the recovered sample contains 61 extra country-years and exact coefficients differ. Replacing the equality indicator materially changes the substantive conclusion and is an explicit sensitivity challenge; the extension’s own robustness is not the original finding’s robustness.
